data.title: Catalyst Watch: Spotlight on the AI trade, core PCE, and Black Friday traffic
data.description:
Welcome to Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch - a breakdown of some of next week's actionable events that stand out. Read more about the events that may impact stock prices next week.

 

Monday - November 23

  • Volatility watch - Micron (MU) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) have seen options volatility increase over the last week. The most overbought stocks per their 14-day Relative Strength Index include Polibeli Group (PLBL), BellRing Brands (BRBR), and Surgery Partners (SGRY). The most oversold stocks per their 14-day Relative Strength Index include Sable Offshore (SOC) and Eagle Nuclear Energy (NUCL). Short interest is elevated again on Six Flags Entertainment (FUN) and Sphere Entertainment (SPHR). Traders will be watching Ambarella (AMBA) closely during earnings week amid M&A speculation.
  • Dividend watch - Companies that have an ex-dividend date coming next week include Hyatt (H), Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), Newmont (NEM), and S&P Global (SPGI).
  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), Agilent (A), and Zoom Communications (ZM).
  • IPO watch - The quiet period expires on Bambusa Therapeutics (BBTX) and Aspen Neuroscience (ASPE) to free up analysts to post ratings. Anthropic (ANT) could also see some new ratings as non-underwriters jump the quiet period gun.
  • Fedspeak - New York Fed President John Williams will deliver prepared remarks followed by a moderated Q&A at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in the Bronx.
  • All day - Preliminary flash PMI readings will be released for major economies, including India, France, Germany, the Eurozone, the UK, and the U.S.

 

Tuesday - November 24

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Dell Technologies (DELL), Analog Devices (ADI), Workday (WDAY), Autodesk (ADSK), Best Buy (BBY), HP (HPQ), Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS), J.M. Smucker (SJM), and Dollar Tree (DLTR). Options trading implies a double-digit share price move for Burlington Stores (BURL) and Ambarella (AMBA) after their reports are released.
  • All day - Piper Sandler will hold a virtual Quantum Day event that will feature participation from Infleqtion (INFQ).
  • M&A votes - Shareholders with Mistras (MG) will vote on the acquisition offer from investment firm H.I.G. Capital. Shareholders with both Transocean (RIG) and Valaris (VAL) will vote on their pending deal.
  • 4:30 p.m. Dell (DELL) will hold its earnings conference call. Major topics will be the AI order backlog, AI-server margins, and the guidance update. Keysight Technologies (KEYS) and NetApp (NTAP) have the highest trading correlation with Dell. Supplier Intel (INTC) derives 19% of its revenue from Dell and moves in tandem with 88% of the time after earnings day.

 

Wednesday - November 25

  • Earnings watch - Notable companies due to report include Deere (DE) and Li Auto (LI).
  • All day - Hershey (HSY) will be on the big screen when a new biopic released by Angel Studios covers the backstory of how Milton Hershey and his wife built the chocolate empire. The film stars Finn Wittrock as Milton and Alexandra Daddario as Kitty, with Mark Waters directing.
  • 8:30 a.m. The November core PCE price index report will be released. Economists forecast an uptick to a 3.2% year-over-year pace for the closely watched inflation gauge. It will be the final inflation print before the FOMC meeting on December 8-9.
  • 8:30 a.m. The November Durable Goods Orders will be released by the U.S. Census Bureau.
  • 8:30 a.m. The second estimate on Q3 GDP will be released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Economists forecast 3.4% growth.
  • 2:00 p.m. The Federal Reserve will release its Beige Book Report. The report will summarize current economic conditions across the Fed's districts.

 

Thursday - November 26

  • All day - The U.S. stock markets will be closed for observance of the Thanksgiving holiday.
  • All day - European leaders meet for a Euro Summit in Brussels.
  • Football feast - The NFL Thanksgiving week slate begins on Wednesday, November 25 with the Green Bay Packers at Los Angeles Rams on Netflix (NFLX), continues on Thanksgiving with Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions (CBS/Paramount+), Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (Fox/Fox One/Tubi), and Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (NBC/Peacock), and concludes on Black Friday, November 27 with Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers on Amazon Prime Video.

 

Friday - November 27

  • All day - Black Friday foot traffic is expected to see a bounce from the last two years even as it remains well below the pre-pandemic levels. In a CivicScience survey, 40% of Black Friday shoppers indicated they plan to shop in person, the highest level since 2014. Notably, Generation Z is forecast to lead the traffic recovery.
  • 1:00 p.m. The U.S. stock markets will close early.

 

Seeking Alpha editor Josh Fineman contributed to this article.

data.title: POET Technologies retreats 15% as tech stocks fall
data.description:
Photonic packaging company POET Technologies (POET) dropped almost 15% on Friday. The stock fell $0.60 to trade at $3.47 in the final hour of trading.

The decline coincided with a broad market selloff. SPY lost almost 3%, QQQ fell almost 5%, and the XLK technology sector ETF slid just over 6%. Optical and AI-infrastructure peers COHR, NBIS, OUST and CRDO each fell more than 13%.

Shares also traded below the 52-week low of $3.87.

data.title: Arista Networks sinks 12% amid tech and AI selloff
data.description:
Networking company Arista Networks (ANET) sank almost 12% on Friday. The stock changed hands at $167.04 as of 2:54pm ET, a decline of $22.55 on the day.

The decline coincided with a broad pullback in technology and AI-linked shares. The technology sector ETF XLK fell almost 7%, QQQ shed almost 5% and SPY lost about 3%. Peers also fell sharply, with AVGO down just over 12%, DELL down just over 11% and ALAB down just over 13%.

data.title: Canadian Solar plunges on report it hired advisers, and may consider bankruptcy
data.description:
Canadian Solar (CSIQ) sank 24% on a report that the solar company and its subsidiary Recurrent Energy are working with advisers to pursue strategic alternatives.

Canadian Solar (CSIQ) is looking at options, including asset sales, financing, and, if necessary, a potential Chapter 11 filing, according to a post on X from OctusCredit, which cited unidentified sources.

The solar provider didn't immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's email request for comment.

Canadian Solar (CSIQ) has short interest of 29%.

The solar company is set to report Q3 results on Dec. 3.

data.title: Everforth climbs 6%, rebounding from recent weakness
data.description:
With the overall market plunging, beaten-down stock Everforth (EFOR) gained just over 6% on Friday. The stock rose $1.81 to trade at $30.84 in the afternoon.

Going into the session, shares had retreated in each of the six previous sessions, including a plunge of 10% on Thursday. Prior to Friday's rally, the stock's five-day return stood at negative 18%, and the one-month return at negative 23%.

data.title: Take-Two says GTA VI posts record $3.79B in day-one sales
data.description:
Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, setting a record for the biggest entertainment launch across any medium, parent company Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) said on Friday.

Take-Two (TTWO) said the game sold 32.5 million units before its official release, setting a record across all platforms. It also claimed a Metacritic score of 99, describing the critical response as widespread acclaim.

The sales figures are based on company estimates through the end of November 19 worldwide, according to the announcement issued by Rockstar Games.

“It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Sam Houser, president and founder of Rockstar Games, said in a statement.

Houser thanked players worldwide for their response to the release and said the company was excited to share the moment with them.

The game is available through the PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store, Rockstar Games Store, and retailers and storefronts worldwide, the company said.

Grand Theft Auto VI carries an M rating for mature audiences from the Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB).

Shares were trading about 5% higher on Friday.

data.title: Microsoft emphasizes 'pay-for-performance' in its Azure cloud division: report
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) management is emphasizing "pay-for-performance" initiatives for employees in its lucrative Azure cloud business, according to Bloomberg.

Employees who demonstrate better performance will receive more benefits, such as additional stock awards, while those with lower performance results will receive higher scrutiny, according to the report, which cited an internal memo.

"Pay-for-performance only works if we are equally rigorous on both sides: recognizing exceptional impact and being honest when performance falls short," said the memo, which was issued by Arun Ulagaratchagan, executive vice president of Azure. 

"Meeting today's bar means closing previous performance gaps and demonstrating a meaningful step-change in impact," he added. "AI is reshaping how the world works, and competition has never been more intense."

"A world-class team like Azure requires world-class talent," a Microsoft spokesperson said, according to the report. "Yesterday, we shared an update to our compensation model in Azure, which includes meaningful additional awards for our strongest performing colleagues. We also shared an update on how we will ensure employees have clear expectations and receive timely, direct feedback from their managers."

Microsoft has focused recently on making the company, which employs more than 220,000 people worldwide, leaner and operate more efficienctly.

Last month, the company began offering a voluntary exit program to eligible employees in the U.S., Canada, India, and the U.K. The buyout program applies to about 60,000 employees. What's more, Azure President Girish Bablani asked senior leaders in his unit to identify ways to reduce costs by at least 20%.

Earlier this year, the company also offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its U.S. workforce, or roughly 9,000 employees. Microsoft cut about 4,800 jobs in July, or roughly 2.1% of its global workforce.
